page: Amazon Web Services m7a.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is powered by a 3.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9R14 processor configured with 4 dedicated x86_64 physical cores, yielding 4 vCPUs at 1 thread per core. Memory capacity is 16.0 GB of DDR5 operating at 5 GHz, providing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio (4.0 GB per core). The instance includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache, along with hardware-level support for vector instructions including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16. The instance does not bundle any local storage or GPUs, relying on remote block storage, and operates with a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core computational execution, with stress-ng single-core performance scoring in the top 25% at 3,077.37. Decompression efficiency is also solid, marked by single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 13.81 GB/sec and Geekbench text processing at 2,668.0, both placing in the top quartile. However, uncached large-block memory bandwidth tests show weaker performance, recording 32.75 GB/sec for 256 MB reads and 25.32 GB/sec for writes, landing in the bottom quartile. General multi-core throughput, static web serving throughput (8.15 GB/sec), PassMark benchmarks (10,567.1 overall CPU), and Redis operations (10.51 million SET ops/sec) remain consistent with mid-tier general-purpose averages.

This hardware balance delivers predictable efficiency for compute and memory loads that prioritize dedicated execution without hyperthreading overhead. It is well suited for web serving fleets, enterprise backend services, small-scale caching layers, and general containerized application deployments.
description: Amazon Web Services m7a.xlarge is a general-purpose instance driven by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and AMD EPYC 9R14 processors. It features 4 dedicated x86_64 physical cores (4 vCPUs) clocked at 3.7 GHz, paired with 16.0 GB of DDR5 RAM running at 5 GHz for a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. Local NVMe storage and GPUs are omitted entirely, and networking provides a 2 Gbps baseline. The processor includes AVX-512 extensions and 16 MB of L3 cache, yielding top-quartile performance in single-core stress-ng tests and bzip3 decompression, alongside mid-range multi-core scores and Redis throughput. Because large-block uncached memory operations fall into the lower quartile, the instance is best suited for balanced enterprise workloads, web application serving, continuous integration tasks, and intermediate microservices rather than memory-streaming workloads.
